questions.skill: Precise definition of a line segment
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Points A and B lie on line ℓ. Which is a precise definition of segment AB?
questions.prompt_markup: Points A and B lie on line ℓ. Which is a precise definition of segment AB?

choices.text: Point A and every point of line ℓ on the same side of A as B
Every point of the plane that is closer to A than to B
Points A and B together with every point C of line ℓ for which AC + CB = AB

questions.correct_answer: Points A and B together with every point C of line ℓ for which AC + CB = AB
questions.grading_note: A segment is its two endpoints and every point between them; "C is between A and B" means C is on the line and AC + CB = AB (distance along a line). The other choices describe line ℓ, ray AB, and a half-plane.

branch.new_demand: Find counterexamples to imprecise segment-based definitions and repair them.
branch.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the definitions written there are tested against counterexamples.

questions.skill: Test segment-based definitions with counterexamples
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Proposed definition: "Point M is the midpoint of segment AB if AM = MB." Give a counterexample, and repair the definition.
questions.prompt_markup:
Proposed definition: "Point M is the midpoint of segment AB if AM = MB."
Give a counterexample, and repair the definition.
questions.correct_answer: The top vertex of an isosceles triangle with base AB has AM = MB but is not on AB. Repair: M is the point ON segment AB with AM = MB.
questions.grading_note: Any counterexample with M off segment AB and AM = MB, plus a repair that puts M on the segment.

questions.correct_answer: Three segments that do not meet end to end (for example three parallel segments). Repair: for noncollinear A, B, C, the segments AB, BC, and CA.

questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Proposed definition: "C is between A and B if AC + CB = AB." Is this enough when A, B, and C are any three points of a plane? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
Proposed definition: "C is between A and B if AC + CB = AB."
Is this enough when A, B, and C are any three points of a plane? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes for the plane: AC + CB = AB forces C onto segment AB (otherwise the triangle inequality gives AC + CB > AB). Many texts still add "C on line AB" for clarity.
questions.grading_note: Any correct explanation using the triangle inequality. Accept "add C on line AB" as a valid repair if the student says why it is safe.
